newsitem.title: UK: TIACA achieving world recognition, says chairman.
newsitem.headline: TIACA achieving world recognition, says chairman.

text.p: The International Air Cargo Association (TIACA) is getting closer to being recognised as the organisation representing airfreight interests worldwide, said chairman and president Chris Foyle.

He said that last week he had meetings with the European Commission's DG 7 transport directorate in Brussels and the International Air Transport Association (IATA) in Geneva to help improve TIACA's global status and image.
He described the talks with DG 7 as successful and that with IATA a "feeling of enmity and antagonism I felt existed between the two associations" was changed to a climate of co-operation.
"The airlines have IATA to represent them, the airports have ACI (Airports Council International) and the forwarders, FIATA," Foyle told Reuters in an interview.

"But TIACA is the only organisation representing international air cargo interests as a whole and I want it to be recognised as such by the likes of IATA, DG 7 and the U.S. Department of Transportation as well as Congress," he said.

He added that TIACA had also recently formed a joint working group with the U.S. shippers' representative body, the National Industrial Transport League. -Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017
